headline.en: Three practitioners. Three small fixes that change everything.
headline.zh: 三位从业者，三个改变一切的小修复。

subtext.en: Teeth, eyes, feet — what most of us take for granted until we can't.
subtext.zh: 牙齿、眼睛、脚 — 多数人不当回事，直到无法忽视。

definition.en: A dental specialist who straightens teeth and corrects bite — the engineer of the smile.
definition.zh: 矫正牙齿与咬合的牙科专科 — 微笑的工程师。

etymology.en: From Greek odous/odont- (tooth) + orthos (straight). The straight-tooth specialist.
etymology.zh: 希腊词根 odous / odont（牙齿）+ orthos（直）。让牙齿变直的专科。

sentences.en: Two years of orthodontist visits and one retainer later — her teenage daughter's smile would stay straight for life.
sentences.zh: 两年的正畸就诊加一副保持器之后 — 女儿青春期的笑容，会整齐一生。

sentences.en: He saved up for adult orthodontist work in his thirties — and quietly noticed how much more often people smiled back.
sentences.zh: 他三十多岁攒钱去做成人正畸 — 然后悄悄发现，别人对他笑的次数多了不少。

mnemonic.en: ORTHODONTIST = orthos (straight) + odont (tooth). The straight-tooth maker.
mnemonic.zh: orthodontist = orthos（直）+ odont（牙）。让牙齿变直的人。

question.en: Orthodontist vs dentist — what's the difference?
question.zh: 正畸医生和普通牙医的区别？

answer.en: Dentist = general dental care (cleaning, fillings, extractions). Orthodontist = a dentist with 2–3 extra years specialized in alignment — braces, aligners, bite correction.
answer.zh: 普通牙医做常规牙科（洁牙、补牙、拔牙）；正畸医生是多读了 2–3 年专攻牙齿排列的牙医 — 牙套、隐形矫正、咬合矫正。

question.en: Why has adult orthodontics become so common?
question.zh: 为什么成人正畸现在这么普遍？

answer.en: Clear aligners removed the social cost — invisible to coworkers, removable for meals. Adults who skipped braces as kids can finally fix what bothered them for decades.
answer.zh: 隐形矫正消除了社交成本 — 同事看不见，吃饭能取下。小时候没戴牙套的成年人，终于可以处理困扰了几十年的事。

anecdote.en: The 45-year-old who got braces alongside her 13-year-old daughter — and said the awkward year of selfies together became one of their best memories.
anecdote.zh: 那位 45 岁和 13 岁女儿一起戴牙套的妈妈 — 她说一起拍的那些尴尬合照，反而成了最珍贵的回忆。

definition.en: A practitioner who measures vision and prescribes corrective lenses — the doctor between you and a clear page.
definition.zh: 测量视力并开具矫正镜片处方的从业者 — 你与一张清晰书页之间的那位医生。

etymology.en: From Greek optos (seen) + metron (measure). Literally 'one who measures sight.'
etymology.zh: 希腊词 optos（所见）+ metron（测量）— 字面意思'测量视觉的人'。

sentences.en: An annual optometrist visit catches drift you don't notice — your eyes adjust until one day they can't.
sentences.zh: 每年一次的验光能发现你察觉不到的变化 — 眼睛一直在适应，直到有一天适应不动了。

sentences.en: Their seven-year-old failed the school eye test — the optometrist found mild astigmatism, and his reading scores jumped within a month.
sentences.zh: 他们七岁的儿子学校视力测试没过 — 验光师查出轻度散光，戴上眼镜一个月，阅读成绩就跳了一大截。

mnemonic.en: OPTOMETRIST = optos (seen) + metron (measure). Same metron in geometry, thermometer, kilometer.
mnemonic.zh: optometrist = optos（所见）+ metron（测量）。geometry、thermometer、kilometer 里都是同一个 metron。

question.en: Optometrist vs ophthalmologist — when do you see which?
question.zh: 验光师和眼科医生 — 什么时候找哪个？

answer.en: Optometrist = vision exams, glasses/contact prescriptions, basic eye health. Ophthalmologist = MD who handles disease, injury, surgery. Start with the optometrist; escalate when needed.
answer.zh: 验光师做视力检查、眼镜或隐形眼镜处方、基础眼部健康；眼科医生是医学博士，处理疾病、外伤、手术。先看验光师，需要时再升级。

question.en: Why is 'optometrist' built on the metron root?
question.zh: 为什么 optometrist 用 metron 这个词根？

answer.en: Their core craft is precise measurement — diopters, axes, prism, pupillary distance. Same Greek 'metron' you see in every measuring word: geometry, barometer, kilometer.
answer.zh: 他们的核心技艺就是精确测量 — 屈光度、轴向、棱镜、瞳距。和所有'测量'词共享同一个 metron：geometry、barometer、kilometer。

anecdote.en: The 60-year-old who finally got progressive lenses — and said the simplest thing changed: he could read a menu without taking off his glasses.
anecdote.zh: 那位 60 岁终于配了渐进镜的人 — 他说一件小事变了：看菜单不用再摘眼镜了。

definition.en: A practitioner who treats foot, ankle, and lower-limb problems — corns, bunions, fallen arches, diabetic foot care.
definition.zh: 治疗足部、踝部及下肢问题的从业者 — 鸡眼、拇外翻、扁平足、糖尿病足部护理。

etymology.en: From Greek podos (foot) + iatros (healer). The foot's specialist.
etymology.zh: 希腊词 podos（脚）+ iatros（医者）— 脚的专科。

sentences.en: After years of ignoring foot pain, his first podiatrist visit identified plantar fasciitis — and a $30 insole fixed what painkillers couldn't.
sentences.zh: 忍了多年脚痛之后，第一次看足科医生就查出足底筋膜炎 — 30 美元的鞋垫解决了止痛药一直没解决的问题。

sentences.en: Their grandfather's diabetes meant podiatrist visits every three months — small checks that prevented the kind of complications nobody wants to think about.
sentences.zh: 他们的爷爷有糖尿病，每三个月要看足科 — 一次次小检查，避开了那种没人愿意去想的并发症。

mnemonic.en: PODIATRIST = podos (foot) + iatros (healer). Same podos in podium (foot-stand) and tripod (three-foot).
mnemonic.zh: podiatrist = podos（脚）+ iatros（医者）。podium（讲台 = 脚下站台）和 tripod（三脚架）里都是同一个 podos。

question.en: Podiatrist vs orthopedist — both treat bones, right?
question.zh: 足科医生和骨科医生 — 都治骨头，对吧？

answer.en: Orthopedist treats the whole musculoskeletal system. Podiatrist specializes specifically in the foot and ankle — corns, bunions, diabetic foot care, custom orthotics. Narrower scope, deeper expertise.
answer.zh: 骨科医生处理整个肌肉骨骼系统；足科医生专攻足部与踝部 — 鸡眼、拇外翻、糖尿病足、定制矫形鞋垫。范围更窄，钻得更深。

question.en: Why does diabetes make podiatry so important?
question.zh: 为什么糖尿病让足科变得这么重要？

answer.en: Diabetes damages nerves and circulation in the feet first — small wounds heal slowly, get infected, and can lead to amputation. Regular podiatrist visits catch problems before they cascade.
answer.zh: 糖尿病最早损伤的是脚部的神经和血液循环 — 小伤口愈合缓慢，容易感染，严重可能导致截肢。定期看足科能在问题级联之前发现。

anecdote.en: The marathon runner who refused podiatrist visits for years — until plantar fasciitis took her out of three races. One pair of custom orthotics later, she ran her first sub-3:30.
anecdote.zh: 那位多年拒绝看足科的马拉松跑者 — 直到足底筋膜炎让她退出三场比赛。一副定制鞋垫之后，她跑出了人生第一个 3:30 以内。

setup.en: Both started by measuring something small.
setup.zh: 都从测量一件小事开始。

leftMnemonic.en: orthos + odont · the straightener of the smile
leftMnemonic.zh: orthos + odont · 微笑的矫正者

rightMnemonic.en: optos + metron · the measurer of vision
rightMnemonic.zh: optos + metron · 视觉的丈量者

closing.en: The smallest measurements often change the most.
closing.zh: 最小的测量，往往带来最大的改变。

reflection.en: We don't notice teeth, eyes, or feet — until they fail. These three are why we get to keep ignoring them.
reflection.zh: 我们平时不会留意牙齿、眼睛、脚 — 直到它们出问题。这三位，让我们可以一直不必留意。

bookRef.author: Norman Lewis
bookRef.theme: How to Talk About Various Practitioners

gloss.en: The branch of dentistry that aligns teeth — the field, not the practitioner.
gloss.zh: 矫正牙齿排列的牙科分支 — 学科本身，而不是从业者。

usage.en: Modern orthodontics is less about metal in the mouth and more about 3D scans and printed aligners.
usage.zh: 现代正畸更多关于 3D 扫描和定制透明矫正器，而不再是嘴里那一堆金属。

gloss.en: Relating to the gums around the teeth — peri (around) + odont (tooth).
gloss.zh: 与牙齿周围的牙龈相关 — peri（周围）+ odont（牙齿）。

usage.en: Periodontal disease is one of the most underrated long-term risks — gums silently recede before teeth start to go.
usage.zh: 牙周病是最被低估的长期健康风险之一 — 牙龈悄悄萎缩，牙齿才开始掉。

gloss.en: The math of shape and space — geo (earth) + metron (measure). Originally 'earth-measuring' for surveying land.
gloss.zh: 形状与空间的数学 — geo（地球）+ metron（测量）。最初是为了测量土地的'量地'学。

usage.en: The Egyptians invented geometry to redraw farm boundaries after the Nile flooded each year — math born of necessity.
usage.zh: 古埃及人发明了几何 — 因为尼罗河每年泛滥之后，要重新画出田地的边界。数学，是被需要逼出来的。

gloss.en: An instrument that measures atmospheric pressure — baros (weight) + metron (measure). Also figurative: a sign of broader change.
gloss.zh: 测量大气压力的仪器 — baros（重量）+ metron（测量）。也常引申为'风向标'。

usage.en: Consumer spending is the barometer most economists watch first — falling confidence shows up in receipts before headlines.
usage.zh: 消费者支出是大多数经济学家首先看的风向标 — 信心下滑会先体现在收据上，然后才登上头条。

gloss.en: An instrument that measures temperature — thermo (heat) + metron (measure).
gloss.zh: 测量温度的仪器 — thermo（热）+ metron（测量）。

usage.en: She kept a thermometer in the nursery — and learned over twenty years that a baby's fever rarely meant what panic suggested.
usage.zh: 她在育儿室里放了一支温度计 — 二十年下来，她渐渐明白：婴儿发烧，很少是恐慌想象的那种事。

gloss.en: The straight measurement across a circle — dia (across / through) + metron (measure).
gloss.zh: 横穿圆心的直线长度 — dia（穿过）+ metron（测量）。

usage.en: A pizza's diameter is the only spec worth comparing — square inches scale fast, and 'large' means very different things at different shops.
usage.zh: 比较披萨大小，直径才是唯一值得看的指标 — 面积按平方涨得快，不同店里'大'的意思差别巨大。

gloss.en: One thousand meters — kilo (thousand) + metron (measure). The unit most of the world runs on.
gloss.zh: 一千米 — kilo（千）+ metron（测量）。世界上多数国家通用的距离单位。

usage.en: Her first 5-kilometer run was harder than her later marathons — beginners feel every step in a way you eventually forget.
usage.zh: 她的第一个 5 公里跑，比后来的马拉松都难 — 新手会感受到每一步，那种感觉以后你会慢慢忘掉。

gloss.en: A raised platform — literally 'a place for the feet,' from Greek podos (foot).
gloss.zh: 升高的台子 — 字面是'放脚的地方'，来自希腊词 podos（脚）。

usage.en: Hours of preparation, three minutes on the podium — most speeches owe more to the writing than to the moment.
usage.zh: 几小时的准备，三分钟在讲台上 — 大多数演讲，靠的不是那一刻，而是之前写出来的东西。

vocabularyExpansion.zh: 对跖点 / 截然相反的事物

gloss.en: The exact opposite point on the globe — anti (against) + podos (foot). The place 'under your feet' all the way through.
gloss.zh: 地球上完全对应的另一点 — anti（反）+ podos（脚）。字面是'脚下穿过去'的那一点。

usage.en: His grandmother in Shanghai and his roommate in Buenos Aires were near antipodes — same clock, opposite seasons.
usage.zh: 他上海的奶奶和布宜诺斯艾利斯的室友差不多是地球的对跖点 — 时钟一致，季节相反。

gloss.en: A three-legged stand — tri (three) + podos (foot). Same podos as podiatrist.
gloss.zh: 三条腿的支架 — tri（三）+ podos（脚）。和 podiatrist 共享 podos 词根。

usage.en: Every photographer eventually buys the expensive tripod they swore they'd never need — the difference is visible from the first sharp shot.
usage.zh: 每个摄影师最终都会买下那台'我永远不需要'的昂贵三脚架 — 拍出的第一张清晰照片就让人明白差别。

gloss.en: Relating to the eye or vision — same Greek optos as optometrist.
gloss.zh: 与眼睛或视觉相关 — 与 optometrist 共享同一个希腊词 optos。

usage.en: The optic nerve is so dense with information that the brain devotes a third of its cortex to processing it.
usage.zh: 视神经携带的信息量极大 — 大脑用了三分之一的皮层来处理它。

gloss.en: Relating to sight or to light-based devices — lenses, fiber, instruments.
gloss.zh: 与视觉或光学设备相关 — 镜头、光纤、光学仪器。

usage.en: Optical illusions reveal not flaws in the eye but assumptions in the brain — what you 'see' is mostly inference.
usage.zh: 光学错觉揭示的不是眼睛的缺陷，而是大脑的假设 — 你'看到的'东西，大半是推断出来的。

gloss.en: A craftsperson who fits and dispenses corrective lenses — works from an optometrist's or ophthalmologist's prescription.
gloss.zh: 根据验光师或眼科医生的处方制作并配戴眼镜的技师。

usage.en: A good optician adjusts the frame on your face for ten minutes — and the glasses you've been fighting all month suddenly disappear.
usage.zh: 一位好的配镜师会花十分钟调整眼镜在你脸上的位置 — 那副和你斗了一个月的眼镜，忽然就'消失'了。
